candidate.name: Edge shape cache entry cap and wholesale clearing
candidate.status: New observational evidence on current main
candidate.proposal: A/B entry-count versus byte/cost bounds and selective retention, preserving a bounded cache. Assess whole-layout time, cache lookup/reshape counts and retained memory. Do not assume LRU alone solves a sequential working set larger than capacity. Do not simply remove bounds.
candidate.validation: Same paragraph at repeated/changed widths, cold/warm contexts, long and short windows, many paragraphs, first-line alternates, variable fonts, saturation and warning/budget equivalence. Cache hits must continue to charge the same reshape budget.

implementation_constraints: Retain only the most recent paragraph identity (id,pointer), clear/reset/shrink releases the map and windows.
Range and glyph budget stay in the key; operation reshape requests charged before lookup, including hits.
Only clean, unedited, unsaturated results eligible; original 1024 glyph-equivalent per-window maximum unchanged.

At most 2048 entries and 1048576 accounted bytes. Account glyph/run Vec capacities, Arc tuple and instance owned coordinates/variations/language/features, with table metadata allowance. Shared instance/features may be overcounted conservatively. Exact allocator overhead/RSS is not bounded by this value.
Full cache refuses admission instead of clearing resident results. Preflight avoids snapshot clone on refusal. Failed replacement preserves previous entry.
Cache hits still deep-copy for independently owned selected output; this optimization does not eliminate that necessary copy.

limitations: Single machine/toolchain/fixed Latin fixture, rather than a whole application speedup or universal benefit.

Resident retention deliberately increases when more short windows fit. Scope start_live_bytes includes unrelated font/paragraph/accepted-output state and can include other context buffers; report the complete process-wide delta rather than attributing every byte to the cache alone.
Initial context/cold preparation and output/drop scopes specified above; no process-startup or font-discovery timing claim.
Wide one-line controls show a small elapsed regression despite identical allocation counts and no edge-window activity; retain that tradeoff explicitly.

At capacity, new windows are reshaped instead of replacing the resident set. A later width hot set may receive fewer hits, while owner change/reset/shrink clears all. Measured width cycling covers three widths, not every transition.
